Subject: Onboarding: offline update & signer flow for Evershore

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this — Evershore is finalizing the acceptance window for their sealed site (Newark COLO). We need to validate two things before we confirm the courier: 1) the manifest signing format you require for on-site ingestion, and 2) the operator ceremony / check-in checklist HarborCloud should expect at the gate.

Two constraints: the site is air-gapped (no outbound networks) and the ops team will only accept signed tar bundles on an approved USB image. They asked for an example manifest + a short checklist they can hand to the courier.

Can your team share the signing scheme (what key types, signature envelope, canonical manifest path), a short acceptance template, and an ETA for a signed test bundle so we can align the courier schedule?

Paul Santos

Subject: RE: Onboarding: offline update & signer flow for Evershore

Paul — thanks, and great to meet you.

Short answer: we use an explicit detached signature model for offline bundles and a canonical manifest schema (yaml) with the following properties:
- Manifest root: /manifest/manifest.yaml (utf-8, stable key ordering)
- Signed with an RSA-4096 detached signature (PKCS#7 acceptable) or an Ed25519 detached sig if customers prefer smaller artifacts
- Signature envelope: {manifest.yaml, signature.sig, public-key.pem} inside the tar.gz top-level directory

I'll attach a short acceptance template you can share with HarborCloud (operator checklist + required fields for manifest ingestion).

Operational plan we propose:
1) Redwood produces a signed test bundle (signed-manifest-v1.2.tar.gz) and shares out-of-band checksum via the buyer PKI (we recommend a pre-shared out-of-band fingerprint over the customer onboarding ticket).
2) Courier delivers USB; HarborCloud runs operator-handshake-checklist.pdf with the on-site operator, verifies the signature and manifest fields offline.
3) If verification passes, operator stages the bundle on the sealed host; we provide a recovery token and activation window.

Proposed dates: we can produce the signed test bundle by EOD 2026-09-22 if HarborCloud can confirm courier ETA for 2026-09-24.

Attaching: acceptance_template.xlsx (simple one-page acceptance + manifest field checklist).

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Vivek / team — quick ops note and a couple of checklist items I want to capture before we sign the bundle:

On the manifest: include fields: version, build_id, components[ {name, hash, size} ], signing_key_id, created_at, expected_install_path, install_user, pre_install_checks (hash of pre-check script). HarborCloud wants a human-readable summary page at /manifest/README.txt with the manifest fingerprint.

On operator ceremony: HarborCloud requires the courier's chain of custody (two signatures on the courier manifest) and operator ID badge verification. The operator-handshake-checklist.pdf covers that — please confirm we add a line for operator phone verification (they call the on-call ops lead at Evershore).

I uploaded an internal test build and produced a signed artifact (signed-manifest-v1.2.tar.gz) for the Newark site. It's a test payload with a fake component blob (md5 stub). I'm attaching the tar stub and the checklist.

Thanks all — confirmed. Courier (FleetSecure) ETA 2026-09-24 08:00 local. HarborCloud Ops has reviewed the acceptance_template.xlsx and the checklist; we will: 
- Verify operator badge + courier chain of custody on arrival
- Run signature verification locally (detached sig check) against the attached public-key.pem provided in the bundle
- Execute the pre-install hash checks and validate README fingerprint before handing the bundle to the sealed host operator

On the out-of-band fingerprint: we will accept a phone call from Evershore on the day of delivery to confirm the SHA256 fingerprint (call to Paul Santos).

Please send the final signed bundle and a copy of public-key.pem to HarborCloud's secure upload link (we will provide a short-lived upload token via our ticketing system) — or, if you prefer, the courier can carry the public-key.pem on a separate USB sealed envelope (preferred by the site security team).

Onboarding contact: Jenna Park — HarborCloud Operations Lead — jenna.park@harborcloud-retail.com
